We walked the LG car park at KLGCC Mall on 9 November 2026.
Five minutes of phone footage, rebuilt as a digital twin of the whole level.
Pillar grid D to U, rows 2 to 7: 261 car bays, 3 of them OKU.
Before: a driver comes in on aisle 3. Every bay they pass is taken.
23 bays are free on aisle 1, but nothing at the entrance says so. Six minutes forty of circling.
After: the twin knows which bays are free, and the entrance sign sends walk-ins to aisle 1.
A booked member drives straight to the Priority Zone by the lifts.
Gate to bay in under a minute, on a quarter of the distance.
How does a booking get accepted? ParkFlow keeps a ledger for the Priority Zone.
Only bays nobody else needs can be promised. At zero, the app offers the next open slot.
At the gate, the plate camera checks the booking in. No ticket, no tap.
The driver parks in any free bay in the zone. The exit plate read ends the booking.
A no-show is held 15 minutes plus 10 minutes' grace, then released to everyone.
Members book free with a voucher. OKU, senior and pram bookings are free. Others pay RM4.
One booking per plate, repeat no-shows pause booking, and unbooked bays stay open to all.
Machine learning does two jobs. A small camera model reads free bays from existing CCTV.
A forecast model predicts occupancy 30 to 90 minutes ahead, from bookings, history and events.
The forecast decides how many bays to hold back. The booking rule decides who gets one.
The member flow: check live space on LG, then book the Priority Zone for an arrival time.
Membership is verified and the voucher applies, so it's free. The bay is held until 2:55.
On the way, the app guides Aina to LG. At the gate, the plate checks the booking in.
Parked by the lifts. First hour free on exit.
The admin dashboard: live occupancy, bookings, arrivals and no-shows in one view.
Every forecast and booking is logged against what actually happened, to prove both work.
It also flags maintenance early: a dirty camera lens, a bay stuck occupied, the next retrain.
ParkFlow. Reserve capacity, not bays.
